newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi's Alujain seeks partners for MTBE plant.
newsitem.headline: Saudi's Alujain seeks partners for MTBE plant.

text.p: Private Saudi Arabian firm Alujain Corp said on Monday it was seeking foreign partners for a proposed 850,000 tonnes a year MTBE plant at Yanbu.
"Alujain Corp is negotiating with two international firms specialised in producing MTBE to participate in the project," a company statement said. It did not name them.
Alujain plans to build the Red Sea coast plant to produce the environmentally-friendly fuel additive methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) which makes gasoline burn more cleanly.
The statement said progress was made in negotiations with all parties involved in the plant, but said "the company would take a decision over the execution of project by October."
A new 525 million riyals ($140 million) company, Tahseen, has been formed to run the proposed plant which was originally scheduled for a 1999 start up.
Finish Energy group Neste Oy has signed a memorandum of understanding with Alujain to become a minority shareholder in the company operating the plant.

Arab Petroleum Investment Corp (APICORP), an affiliate of the Organisation of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC), has also been reported to have an interest in securing a 10 percent stake in Tahseen.
Alujain said talks with international firms who had bid for the main project works were progressing and said it was expected to choose the best bid in two weeks. It gave no details.

ABB Lummus Global Inc, a U.S. affiliate of Switzerland's ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG, Stone & Webster, and Snamprogetti, a unit of Italian ENI, have been in negotiations for the contract to build the plant.
The Jeddah-based company was also studying plans to raise its paid-in capital to 320 million riyals to help finance new projects, the statement said, but gave no further details.
